title: When the Oath Sings Again
premise: Sebastian Oyelaran has spent her life as warden of the Hollow Gate, the sealed door between a godless valley and a country that was erased from every map two centuries ago. When prayers start being answered again, she learns the old gods are not returning on their own: something behind the gate is feeding them power through her oath. To stop the slow burning of the last dragon-fire that keeps both worlds alive, Sebastian must leave the valley for the first time, cross the ghost-country of Vael with a disgraced priest and a deserter knight who loves her, and discover that the gate was never built to keep magic out — it was built to keep her in. In the end she must choose between renewing the oath that preserves the valley and breaking it to let the gods die honestly, singing the door shut herself at the cost of never going home.
about_author: Astrid Underhill is a former archivist of border-town folklore who grew up in a valley so remote its church bells were rung by hand because no signal ever reached it. She writes fantasy about doors, oaths, and the people paid to stand between them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. On the eve of the Oath-Renewal festival, Sebastian performs her duties as gatekeeper: oiling hinges that never open, reciting words she doesn't understand. A child's prayer spoken near the gate is answered — impossibly. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath ritual comfort.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Dragon-fire ash drifts into the valley for the first time in living memory; crops silver over overnight. The village elders blame Sebastian's laxness. She finds a scorched feather-shaped scale fused to the gate itself. Emotional beat: guilt and defensiveness.

chapters.title: A Priest Without a God
chapters.summary: POV Ivo Marren, a defrocked priest exiled to the valley years ago. He confesses to Sebastian that he once served the old gods of Vael and recognizes the answered prayers as their voice. He begs her to open the gate. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of shared exile.

chapters.title: What the Oath Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Touching the gate during renewal rites, Sebastian hears the original oath sung in a dead language — and realizes it names her bloodline as its binding, not its guardian. The gate answers her doubt with a crack of light. Emotional beat: identity shaken.

chapters.title: The Deserter at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel Vane, a knight who deserted the king's army rather than burn a temple. He arrives hunting rumors of answered prayers and recognizes Sebastian's name from forbidden records. Emotional beat: mutual recognition between people who broke rules for mercy.

chapters.title: Doors Do Not Open From This Side
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The three test the gate; it will not open outward. Ivo reveals the truth: the valley is the inside of sealed Vael, and the only exit lies across the ghost-country where the last dragon still burns. Emotional beat: vertigo — home revealed as prison.

chapters.title: Leaving
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian slips the valley at night, leaving her deputy the oath-words and a lie about a pilgrimage. Crossing the threshold, magic floods back into her senses painfully. Emotional beat: grief and exhilaration braided together.

chapters.title: The Country With No Name
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. The party crosses Vael: roads that remember being walked, villages of echoes replaying their final days. Kestrel maps their route while hiding that his desertion happened here. Emotional beat: haunted wonder.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Badly
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. They reach a shrine where a farmer's wish for rain drowned his whole village in standing water. Ivo understands the gods are answering without judgment or limit — they are starving, indiscriminate. Emotional beat: horror at divinity unbound.

chapters.title: The Knight's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Ambushed by remnants of the order he deserted, Kestrel admits he burned nothing but let others burn it; his shame drove him to the valley's edge. Sebastian chooses to trust him anyway. Emotional beat: love kindling in honesty.

chapters.title: The Choir of Small Gods
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. In a ruined cathedral, minor gods — hearth-spirits, road-wights — beg the party to carry them toward the dragon-fire before it gutters out. Sebastian refuses; one follows anyway, hidden in her lantern. Emotional beat: compassion versus caution.

chapters.title: The King's New Gods
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. They learn the crown has been capturing answered prayers, caging small gods to weaponize miracles. Kestrel's former commander leads the hunt — and knows exactly where the party is headed. Emotional beat: dread of institutional corruption.

chapters.title: What Was Done to Vael
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In an archive of living books, Ivo reads the true history: Vael wasn't destroyed by war but sealed away by its own priests to starve the gods, using the first Oyelaran as the lock. Emotional beat: fury at ancestors' cowardice.

chapters.title: The Lock and the Key
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sebastian confronts what she is: not a keeper but the mechanism, her life-force feeding the seal. Renewing the oath yearly has been slowly killing her; the dragon-fire is failing because she is. Emotional beat: betrayal by her own body.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ash Road
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. The commander's riders attack; the stowaway hearth-god reveals itself to save them, burning out most of its essence. Kestrel takes a wound meant for Sebastian. Emotional beat: sacrifice hardening resolve into love.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. At Mount Cindral's caldera they find the dragon — ancient, half-blind, barely alight — sustaining the boundary between existence and erasure. It speaks to Sebastian in the oath-language: finish the work, or undo it. Emotional beat: awe and terrible choice.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Embers
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The dragon offers terms: feed it the caged gods' stolen fire to reignite, and Vael lives sealed forever; or let it die, and the old gods return unfettered to a world unready. Ivo argues for freedom; Sebastian hears her valley's voices in the flames. Emotional beat: philosophy become urgent.

chapters.title: Storming the Reliquary
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. The party raids the crown's reliquary-fortress to free the caged gods before deciding anything. Kestrel faces his commander and refuses to kill him, breaking the cycle that made him. Emotional beat: justice outside law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: When the Oath Sings
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Freed gods pour into the dying dragon like wind into embers — and the oath within Sebastian rises to meet them, singing through her. She finally understands the third option no one recorded: a new oath, freely given, neither seal nor cage. Emotional beat: transcendence.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Climax. At the caldera's heart, Sebastian sings the new oath — binding herself to the door rather than the wall. The gate reopens: the valley rejoins the world, the gods return limited by consent, and the dragon sleeps at last. Emotional beat: triumph laced with irrevocable loss.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Changed
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. The valley wakes to seasons it never had; villagers greet Sebastian as both stranger and daughter. Kestrel chooses to stay at her side, and Ivo takes up a priesthood of honest, unanswered prayer. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Walks Through
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Epilogue. Years later, Sebastian keeps the now-open gate — greeting travelers, teaching children the oath as song instead of chain. Some nights the dragon's ember glows on the horizon, and she sings back. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept.
